$comment: Modelling parameters for the synthetic-data generator, kept separate from
the vocabulary so the shape of demand can be tuned without touching names.
Volumes and the random seed are NOT here — they are operator settings and
SEED_MONTHS, SEED_END_DATE). Everything in this file describes how a sale
behaves, and changing it changes the dataset even at an identical seed.
$commentCategoryDemand: How often a category is chosen for an order line. Deliberately uneven:
uniform demand makes a sales-by-category chart look like noise, and hides
whether the aggregation is actually working.
$commentSeasonality: Multiplier applied to an order's chance of landing in a given calendar
month, so the daily-revenue chart has a recognisable shape instead of a
flat band. The October/November peak stands in for the Indian festive
season; February is the post-festive trough.
$commentWeekday: Monday is 1, Sunday is 7. Weekend retail runs hotter, which gives the
time series a weekly rhythm a reviewer can actually see.
$commentBasket: Distribution of line counts per order. Most baskets are small; a long tail
of larger ones exercises multi-item order handling and makes average order
value non-trivial. Weights are relative, not percentages.
$commentQuantity: Quantity per line. Overwhelmingly single units, which is what keeps
revenue driven by price mix rather than by quantity outliers.
$commentRepeatCustomers: Share of orders placed by the loyal minority. With repeatShare 0.55 and
loyalShare 0.2, one fifth of customers place roughly 55% of orders, so
top-customer analysis has something to find and dim_customer joins are
$commentPricing: A line's sale price is the catalogue price nudged within these bounds, so
unit_price_at_sale genuinely diverges from products.unit_price and the
warehouse's use of the historical price is observable rather than
theoretical. discountChance is the probability of any adjustment at all.
$commentStatus: Order status mix. Older orders are more likely to have reached delivered;
the generator applies these weights only to orders old enough to qualify.
cancelled stays rare but present, so status filtering has real data.
$commentInactiveProducts: Share of the catalogue retired after launch. Inactive products may not be
added to new orders but must keep their historical sales, which is exactly
the case that proves unit_price_at_sale and ON DELETE RESTRICT matter.
